context: A dad reads a fantasy tale to his son
purpose: Teach: 猿/泥棒/架空/はなし/まくる/られれ/生ん/日本一

lines.speaker: ryosuke_dad
lines.jp: 翔、今夜は架空のはなしを読もうか。
lines.en: Sho, how about we read a made-up story tonight?
lines.style: Gentle opening, easy warmth. Inviting rather than announcing. Soft, unhurried pace. The voice of a father who has time and is genuinely present.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: うん!猿の王様、出てくる?
lines.en: Yeah! Does the monkey king come in it?
lines.style: Bright, immediate eagerness. The 'yeah' leaps out. A small child's complete trust that the answer will be yes, that this will be good. Bouncy on the question.

lines.speaker: ryosuke_dad
lines.jp: 登場する。泥棒団もいて、ハラハラする。
lines.en: He does. There's a band of thieves too—keeps you on the edge of your seat.
lines.style: Warm enthusiasm, painting the picture. The confirmation feels like a gift being handed over. Slight dramatic lift on 'thieves' to show he's building anticipation. Not overselling it.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: お父さん、いつもページめくるの早すぎ。読みまくる!
lines.en: Dad, you always turn the pages way too fast. You just barrel through them!
lines.style: Gentle mockery, affectionate complaint. A small laugh underneath. Not angry—familiar enough to tease. The exasperation of someone who's noticed this a hundred times and loves him for it anyway.

lines.speaker: ryosuke_dad
lines.jp: ふふ、終盤、主人公が地に堕ちられればおしまいだぞ。
lines.en: Heh—well, at the end, if the hero gets knocked down, that's the game, right?
lines.style: Playful deflection with a dad-smile in the voice. Light, teasing back. Not defensive—turning it into part of the story itself. A small laugh breaks the line open.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: お母さんが弟を生んだ夜にも、お話、読んでくれたよね。
lines.en: You read to me the night Mom had my little brother too.
lines.style: Quieter. A memory surfacing—not sad, but tender. The voice of a child who understands something about that night mattered. Small, gentle, almost wondering. Trailing slightly on 'too.'

lines.speaker: ryosuke_dad
lines.jp: そうだったな。日本一の絵本作家になりたいって、お前、言ってた。
lines.en: I did. You told me that night you wanted to be Japan's greatest picture-book author.
lines.style: Warm recollection. The tone of a father holding something small and true his child said once. Not teasing—respecting the memory. Gentle, almost wondering at it himself. Slow enough to let it breathe.
